text.p: Turkish central bank's overnight funding fell on Thursday, but its tomorrow value loans to banks rose sharply as cash squeeze continued ahead of Friday's hefty public sector salary payments, bankers said.
But t-bill yields eased on buying prompted by easing liquidity shortage and the announcement of Treasury's first ever reverse auction for Monday to buy back bills having December 10 maturity.

The money market opened only 16.6 trillion lira short on Thursday, down sharply from 121 trillion on Wednesday, so the central bank's overnight lending at 74 percent fell to 8.6 trillion lira from yesterday's 15.4 trillion.

But its tomorrow value funding rose sharply to 29.7 trillion lira at 73 percent on tom/next and 17.5 trillion lira at 74 percent on tom/week, from Wednesday's 22.7 trillion lira tom/next and 4.4 trillion lira tom/week.
The average overnight money and repo rates were 73.79 and 79.79 percent, little changed from Wednesday's 73.85 and 79.84 percent, respectively.

The yield on the most heavily traded and last auctioned August 5, 1998 dropped to 117.62 percent from yesterday's 118.73 and the second most heavily traded paper, July 29, 1998 yielded 117.91 percent, down from previous 118.76.
Bankers said the market wellcomed the Treasury's decision to open a reverse auction to buy back December 10 bills as part of its plan to better organise domestic debt repayments.
There are 380.1 trillion lira of outstanding bills to mature on December 10.

The Turkish lira continued to firm in line with the falling dollar/mark parity. Banks' dollar bids closed at 163,250-300 lira, compared to the interbank close of 163,390 on Wednesday. No dollar deals were made on the central-bank brokered interbank.
The central bank set its key dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 163,300 lira at close, unchanged from Wednesday.
